results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec

All 63 outline units after the five intro callouts match their aligned spec paragraphs' controlling ideas in spec order (p01-p63, including p27/p14 inside Phase 2 and p31-p35 after the Aftermath); callouts match no spec paragraph.
The reverse outliner marked no unit as holding two ideas.

Every unit ties to E1-E6: portfolio (E1), shared layers (E2), brand engineering incl. mobile.de ranking (E3), sale and aftermath (E4), reading rules, timeline and gaps (E5), rules, comparison and questions (E6).

results.draft_locus: Aftermath: Removing a Parent from a Platform ¶2
results.quote: Kijiji is still listed among Adevinta's brands as of October 2026.
results.finding: The €147 million Kijiji Canada impairment is given with no sentence saying what it shows (the spec's 'a kept brand outside the core'); the next paragraph returns to domains and logos, so the statistic's point is left to the reader. Both flow readers could not see why it was there.
All paragraph-level and section-level transitions except the Trade-offs section boundary express the declared relationship and pick up the declared known information; the hand-off links to case-aviv.

results.quote: The rows differ mainly in
results.finding: The section opens directly with the options table; the only prose comes after it and starts from 'The rows'. The declared conclusion_summary phrase carrying over 'the record across all phases' into 'the options set side by side' is absent at the section start.

results.quote: To answer them, the chapter sets reading rules and a timeline
results.finding: Both flow readers had to look back to find what 'them' refers to: the three questions sit mid-p03 and sentences on scope and case-adevinta intervene. Naming the questions would fix it.
results.corroborated_by: Flow reader B, section (3) first item ('Intro: "To answer them..."'); Flow reader A, section (3) second item

results.draft_locus: Phase 2 ¶12, INFERENCE callout after the layer map
results.quote: the regulator needed eBay to offer transitional services to the buyer of Gumtree UK

results.corroborated_by: Flow reader B, section (3) item 'Inference callout after the layer map'; Flow reader A, section (3) fifth item

results.quote: by 2019 it held more than 34 million live ads and took up to a million new ads a day
results.finding: The same figures ('up to a million new ads a day' twice, '34 million' three times) recur across three consecutive paragraphs, and both readers re-read to check whether they were different numbers.

results.draft_locus: Aftermath: Removing a Parent from a Platform ¶1, third bullet
results.quote: Kleinanzeigen's 2025 whole-platform migration, described in the next section, is not documented as a consequence of the sale, and this chapter does not claim it was one.
results.finding: Offered as one of 'three pieces of evidence' of what stopping being eBay took, then disclaimed as not linked to the sale; it also introduces statement-based binary logs before the section that explains them. Both readers found it out of place. The spec requires this migration as the Aftermath's third piece of evidence and as the hand-over to the Berlin section, so the difficulty comes from the declared structure.
results.corroborated_by: Flow reader B, section (3) item 'Aftermath, third bullet'; Flow reader A, section (3) seventh item

results.quote: The Aftermath's third piece of evidence, Kleinanzeigen's whole-platform migration, is documented by its own engineers.
results.finding: Both readers marked the section's position unclear: it is introduced as Aftermath evidence and at once cut loose from the sale, making a loop with the Aftermath bullet. Both proposed moving the 2025 migration next to the Phase 2 Kleinanzeigen subsection or making it a separate 'later engineering' section. The spec's flow and section transition declare exactly this hand-over, so the fault is the order.
results.corroborated_by: Flow reader B, section (2) 'Inside the Berlin Platforms, Replacing the whole platform: unclear placement' and section (3) item 'Inside the Berlin Platforms'; Flow reader A, section (2) 'Inside the Berlin Platforms: unclear' and section (3) tenth item

results.quote: mobile.de, the other Berlin brand, published less about its platform and more about models.
results.finding: Both readers found the mobile.de ranking subsection unconnected to the chapter's three questions (shared, local, sale) and marked its placement unclear; both pointed to the motors/verticals material where it is later cited. The spec places it here as 'a second, narrower example of a brand on its own path'; a bridge to the 'what stayed local' question might mitigate, but both readers' difficulty is the placement.
results.corroborated_by: Flow reader B, section (2) 'Inside the Berlin Platforms, mobile.de ranking: unclear' and section (3) item 'mobile.de ranking subsection'; Flow reader A, section (3) eleventh item

Every does_not_know term is given at first use: Voyager (p18), PanteraS (p20), MoVe (p22), Online Payment Platform and Gelijk Oversteken (p25), undertakings in lieu (p38), TSA (p39). Common Ground and the Veldmark scenario names are on already_knows (meet-veldmark); statement-based binary logs, VIP, LTR and GTIDs are glossed inline.
Opens on the OLX contrast and eBay's 2004-2021 arc (intriguing example), then the silence-as-evidence claim, questions and roadmap; none of the weak patterns.
No 'in conclusion', no new idea or evidence; synthesis plus hand-off.
p62 joins the three questions into one interface-type answer and says why it matters: a register and written interfaces cost little now and keep a group free to keep, merge or sell each brand.
p62 returns to the hook (leaders bought in 2004 and left on their own platforms moved to a new owner) and to the group's silence.

The intro reader predicted the three questions (shared/layer/interface, local, sale revealed), the scattered evidence (Amsterdam and Berlin blogs, GitHub, talks, job postings, regulator, silence as evidence), the mirror image of Adevinta with post-2021 strategy left to case-adevinta, every roadmap section in order, and the ending in rules, Veldmark/Common Ground test and questions.

The cold reader classified the jointly chosen engine (agreement), the external payment provider and the published dealer API (MoVe-style contract) as clean, the parent-owned undocumented fraud service as the Gumtree UK transitional-services case, and named the per-brand dependency register with owner and replacement path and a written interface a third party could operate, matching expected.
